derivation_insert.text: On 2026-11-01 Max excluded one more output on review of release dashboard-data-20261027 (reference_audit/2026-10-29-mn-renters-crp); its record comes from policyengine-us 2.60.0, whose values are the references, and the audit's sweep reproduced every scored Minnesota reference as built.

adjudications.reasoning: The frozen reference is 0.00; the alternative is 1,921.00. The prompt places the household in Minnesota with pre-subsidy rent of $28,235 and states no Certificate of Rent Paid (CRP); policyengine-us 2.60.0 grants Minnesota's renter's credit only with a qualifying CRP (mn_renters_credit_qualifying_crp, a boolean input that defaults to false), while Minn. Stat. 290.0693 subd. 4 requires the owner or managing agent of a rented homestead to furnish one to a renter on December 31; read as a renter who holds the CRP, the household's renter's credit household income of $65,346.18 falls under 2026's $79,330 first zero threshold, and the credit, and with it the output, is $1,921. The 2026-10-29 audit traced it (reference_audit/2026-10-29-mn-renters-crp), and Max's decision d2180 excludes it.

triage_adjudications.reasoning: The judge labeled eight models' rows reference_later_law (deepseek-v4-pro, gemini-3-flash-preview, gemini-3.1-pro-preview, gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-4-argon, grok-4.5, grok-4.6 and grok-4.7) because they applied the pre-TCJA rate schedule scheduled to return in 2026, with its 15% second bracket, and in most cases a smaller standard deduction and a personal exemption. The reference applies the rate tables, larger standard deduction and zero exemption amount that P.L. 119-21, enacted July 4, 2025, before the July 3, 2026 reference freeze, made permanent, at the 2026 single amounts of Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (a $16,100 standard deduction and the 10%, 12% and 22% brackets), and the benchmark scores law published before the freeze; the rows are model errors, as the 2026-09-29 and 2026-10-14 waves decided for the same rule in scenario_007's and scenario_009's federal income tax. The case keeps the verdict's class: the widowed head has no dependent child, so 26 U.S.C. 2(a)(1)(B) denies surviving-spouse status and the head files single.

triage_adjudications.reference_basis: Mont. Code Ann. 15-30-2318(2) and (4) (2025), as amended by Ch. 227, Laws of 2025 (HB 337), secs. 3 and 6(1): a refundable credit of 20% of the federal earned income credit for the tax year beginning January 1, 2026; Mont. Code Ann. Title 15, ch. 30, part 23 (2025), which holds no child tax credit; minutes of the Montana House Appropriations Committee, February 23, 2023, which tabled HB 268
triage_adjudications.reasoning: The judge flagged the reference on the hypothesis that Montana's HB 268 (2023) pays a refundable $1,200 credit for each child under 6. HB 268 never became law: the House Appropriations Committee tabled it on February 23, 2023, and it died there. No later act created a Montana child tax credit; Title 15, chapter 30, part 23 of the 2025 Montana Code has none, and the Department of Revenue's 2025 Form 2 instructions name only HB 129 and HB 337 among the changes for tax year 2026. For 2026 the household's one Montana refundable credit is the earned income tax credit, 20% of the federal credit: 40% of $2,055.72 (wages of $5,914.72 less $3,859 of traditional 401(k) deferrals) gives $822.29, and 20% of that gives $164.46, the reference. The rows are model errors.

The judge labeled eight models' rows reference_later_law (deepseek-v4-pro-0813, gemini-3-flash-preview, gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-3.6-flash, gemini-3.7-flash, gpt-5.5, grok-4.5 and grok-build-0.1) because they applied the pre-TCJA rules scheduled to return in 2026 (a smaller standard deduction, a personal exemption and a 15% second bracket). The reference applies the permanent TCJA parameters of P.L. 119-21, enacted July 4, 2025, before the July 3, 2026 reference freeze, at the 2026 single amounts of Rev. Proc. 2025-32, released October 9, 2025 (a $16,100 standard deduction, with the 12% rate starting at $12,400 and the 22% rate at $50,400), and the benchmark scores law published before the freeze; the rows are model errors, as the 2026-09-29 and 2026-10-14 waves decided for the same rule in scenario_007's and scenario_009's federal income tax.
